page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth scaling. The instance achieved average ratings in stress-ng single-core CPU performance with a score of 1561.99 and Geekbench single-core testing at 1807.0. However, multi-core execution, such as Geekbench multi-core at 4100.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 3213.05, falls into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds of 32.36 GB/sec and 21.01 GB/sec respectively.

Despite these multi-core limitations, the CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions, which assist in specialized workloads. This is reflected in average performance for single-threaded gzip compression at 28.23 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation at 118.57 tokens/sec. Conversely, database operations, software compilation, and Redis SET operations perform in the lower quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-4 offers a standard resource profile suitable for entry-level general-purpose workloads. It is best utilized for static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications where high-throughput multi-core processing and high memory bandwidth are not critical requirements.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores and hyperthreading. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0 and stable static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as uncached memory reads at 32.36 GB/sec and a Passmark CPU score of 6010.98, fall into the lower performance tier. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which assist with lightweight vector and matrix operations. Qualitatively, the n4-standard-4 represents a balanced, budget-friendly option for workloads that do not demand intensive multi-threaded scaling. It is best suited for static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications.
